literal: Thinking 'we are old friends' and doing things that are not proper conduct, such intimacy will yield ruin.
translation: Taking liberties by thinking 'we are old friends' and doing improper things will bring ruin.
modern: நாம் அரசருக்குப் பழைய நண்பர்கள் என்று கருதி, பண்பற்ற செயல்களைச் செய்யும் உரிமை ஒருவருக்கு அழிவையே தரும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against taking undue liberties with a ruler based on long-standing friendship. The word 'பழையம்' captures the presumption of a person who thinks their old ties grant them special privileges. When this presumed intimacy ('கெழுதகைமை') leads someone to act improperly, it will ultimately result in their own ruin. A wise person maintains respectful boundaries regardless of how long they have known the king.
